A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Alberta Wells Dataset. Their main text, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and object-detection experiments in Tables 4–5, qualitative predictions, and analyses of the constructed dataset.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds backbone comparisons, modality and training-composition ablations, and dataset analyses.

M1.justification: The dataset construction, annotation procedure, and clustering-based splitting algorithm remain unchanged. ConvNeXt additions are benchmark comparators; the newly stated four-channel initialization details do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Tables 6–7 add an RGB-only input scenario alongside RGB+NIR. Geographic coverage, well populations, and binary segmentation/detection tasks remain unchanged. The approximately 188,000 total patches clarified in v2 were already documented in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds UperNet with ConvNeXt-Small and ConvNeXt-Base alongside the retained Swin Small configuration. All original segmentation comparators and the four object-detection comparators remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds RGB-only versus four-band controls and active-only versus all-well-type training, together with the additional ConvNeXt configurations and computational-cost reporting. Existing splits, augmentation settings, training budgets, and accuracy metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 directly tests two defining dataset choices: NIR inclusion for segmentation and detection, and inclusion of suspended/abandoned wells in segmentation training. These substantially extend the diagnostic evidence beyond v1's backbone comparisons. Appendix B.4 also adds well-type breakdowns and geographic-density analysis; existing sample illustrations are retained.

E5.justification: Matched benchmark results retain the same unexplained ± reporting. Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new modality results follow the existing convention; Table 8 provides point estimates without documenting another uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: Original Tables 4–5 accuracy values are retained apart from equivalent rounding. Substantial new results include ConvNeXt-Small/Base IoUs of 59.4/59.7, RGB-only segmentation IoU of 56.6 versus 58.0 with NIR, and separate active-only/all-type training IoUs of 0.502/0.576 in Table 8. Parameter counts, GFLOPs, and finer dataset statistics are also added.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1's mathematical specification and imbalance-correction expression are unchanged, as are the metric definitions. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and central dataset contributions remain substantively unchanged. However, the conclusion changes its most promising segmentation baseline from U-Net/EfficientNetB6 to UperNet/ConvNeXt, despite Table 4 and Section 5.1 still favoring U-Net/EfficientNetB6.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations about active-only training's limited generalization, possible advantages over human identification, overlapping annotations, and computational efficiency. The principal limitations remain unchanged. The new claim that ConvNeXt-Small requires fewer parameters than Swin Small conflicts with Table 4's 128.29M versus 81.15M.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly discloses ImageNet initialization and modification of initial layers for four-channel imagery; Tables 4–5 add model-size and computation details. Initialization remains ambiguous because the same passage also says training is from scratch. Dataset formats, processing instructions, access information, and licensing terms are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SpaceNet 7 and distinguishes its urban-monitoring purpose from well detection. References to Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition and Fixing Weight Decay Regularization in Adam are removed, although ResNet and AdamW remain used. Overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted paragraph edits, promotes Results from Section 4.3 to Section 5, adds an Impact Statement, rewrites acknowledgments, and reorders the licensing, dataset-information, examples, and challenges appendices. Most explanatory text and the datasheet remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displays with ablation Tables 6–8, detailed statistics Tables 11–13, and well-type and density Figures 5–6. It redraws Figure 3, adds cost columns to Tables 4–5, consolidates Table 2 columns, and relocates existing displays. Earlier sample illustrations are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The new ablations provide useful empirical support for NIR imagery and mixed-well-type training, while the appendix gives readers a fuller account of dataset composition. These are modest gains over v1. Their benefit is limited by new inconsistencies: the conclusion's ConvNeXt recommendation conflicts with Section 5.1/Table 4, the parameter-efficiency claim contradicts its table, and the initialization disclosure remains ambiguous.
